claim: For every integer \(N\ge2\), reserve \(r\in(0,1)\), and common valuation \(V>0\), the complete-information all-pay auction with bids in \([0,1]\), eligibility only for bids \(b\ge r\), full payment of every bid, and uniform tie-breaking has a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium. For \(V>r\), its continuous bidding component exists exactly when \(V<V_c(N,r)\), where \(V_c(N,r)=N/S_N(q_c)=r/q_c^{N-1}\), \(S_N(q)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}q^j\), and \(q_c\in(0,1)\) uniquely solves \(rS_N(q_c)=Nq_c^{N-1}\). For fixed \(r\), \(V_c(N,r)\to r+a_r\) as \(N\to\infty\), where \(a_r>0\) uniquely solves \(r(e^{a_r}-1)=a_r\).

correctness.rationale: The proof checks every bid region, derives the continuous-support CDF from zero-payoff indifference, derives the cap atom from the binomial tie probability, proves uniqueness of the cutoff, and obtains the limit by Riemann sums. Boundary cases V≤r, V=1, V=Vc, V=N, and V>N are handled explicitly.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification of the symmetric equilibrium and a non-obvious finite large-population cutoff. It quantifies when a continuous range of bids disappears under the joint reserve-and-cap policy, rather than merely recomputing a known two- or three-player table.
